## Pen and Paper: Walk It By Hand Before the Lecture

Do this *before* the lecture. It is designed so that you discover the
stationary distribution yourself, with nothing but a pencil: you fill in a
transition matrix by hand, push a distribution forward step by step, and notice
what the numbers settle on before anybody tells you the formula.

- [Where Does the Drunkard Sleep?](pen-and-paper/exercise.pdf): transition probabilities, one- and two-step distributions, and the long-run visit frequencies of a four-node network.

## Interactive Demos

- [Ladder Lottery](../assets/vis/amida-kuji.html): a fixed board, an unpredictable outcome. Add rungs and watch where you land become a coin flip.
- [Random walk simulator](../assets/vis/random-walks/index.html): the karate club by default. Then run it on a network with [two obvious communities](../assets/vis/random-walks/index.html?dataFile=two-cliques.json) and count how long the walker stays on one side.

## Assignments

Neither graded assignment runs in this module. The [Pair Notebook](../course/pair-notebook.qmd) covers Modules 1 through 6, and the [Group Mini-Project](../course/mini-project.qmd) covers Modules 2 through 6. The worksheet and the notebook above are practice, not submissions.
